public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 7

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos7

open Set

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_7 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i,
      ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos7

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses integer ideals as moduli and expresses oddness as non-containment in Ideal.span {2}, rather than using positive integer moduli and an explicit parity predicate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ideal of ℤ has a unique nonnegative generator m. The CoveringSystem fields ne_bot and ne_top require m > 1. Injectivity of the ideals is equivalent to distinctness of these positive generators. The containment (m) ≤ (2) holds exactly when 2 divides m, so its negation is precisely oddness. The set {a} + (m) is the congruence class a modulo m; unionCovers and the Fintype index express a finite covering of every integer. Conversely, any finite distinct odd covering with moduli greater than 1 constructs such a StrictCoveringSystem. The explicit non-top conjunct is redundant with the structure's ne_top field. A full equivalence with the ordinary finite-family formulation was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem theorem or sorry.
